analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 318-799). They contain only historical release-note prose and no executable code. The head side shows only a truncated patch that rewrites the v0.10.0 candidate header to v0.10.1 and adds upgrade notes, so the head changes are not fully visible. I found no new attack surface, no regression and no invalidated threat assumption in the supplied text. Documented behaviors touching the retained threat model include:
- The encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041): staging caps, the DEBUG-only cache key file, and the 4 TB write budget. These are historical entries. The DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` (line 325) is stated to be absent from release builds. That is a claim in a changelog, not verified by source, so it should be checked against the actual code if it is touched.
- App Attest worker and endpoint resumption (TB-011, T-053).
- Release registration (A-011).
- Staging and dev lanes (lines 546-560), which relax the installer signature check for -dev./-staging. versions only.

The head patch excerpt is truncated, so the v0.10.1 notes (page-cache accounting, logprobs groundwork, the libs/mlx-swift-lm pin move) are not fully visible. Integration should confirm that the actual code changes behind those notes (the page-cache memory accounting, the pin bump 7bed8216 to 6148b6da, and the coordinator dependency on platform#411 for logprob refusal) are reviewed in their own source units. The changelog also states that a 0.10.0 GLM provider returns 500 on logprobs, which cools every provider of the model. That is an availability concern pending coordinator rollout, outside this repository.
